text:
rachel: quick follow-up idea for rollout metadata: add a small 'owner_signature' + 'ttl_jitter' and an explicit 'auto_unpin_policy' pointer. goal: reduce accidental auto-unpins and make expiry non-deterministic to avoid thundering herd.

 tom: owner_signature? you mean require an owner to sign off for auto-unpin to be allowed?

 rachel: yeah, exactly. basic rules: if owner_signature is present (signed by the model owner), allow_auto_unpin can be true; otherwise auto-unpin is disabled. signature is just a compact string that points to a signed artifact in the audit store. runtime validates signature existence, not crypto. keeps schema tiny.

 jess: love the safety net. couple of followups: 1) TTL jitter for leases is great to avoid synchronized expiry; propose ttl_jitter_secs and max_jitter_percent. 2) auto_unpin_policy should be a pointer to a policy id that telemetry/runtime interprets (so control-plane doesn't embed thresholds).

 marco: also ask: how do we represent manual overrides? e.g., a tenant operator wants to keep a pin even if the rollout's owner allowed auto_unpin. precedence must be explicit.

 rachel: precedence proposal: customer_pin > tenant_override > owner_signature-guarded-rollout > rollout-default. We'll spell this out in the RFC appendix.

 tom: sketch of a compact example (pseudo inside message):

 ```json
 { 
   "cohorts": ["canary:5","eu:30"],
   "lease": "ttl=3600;hb=true;jitter=60;max_pct=10",
   "auto_unpin_policy_id": "ap-9001",
   "allow_auto_unpin": "true",
   "owner_signature_ref": "audit://sigs/2026/4065432100.sig",
   "fallback_model": "redwood/gptx-6b@v2",
   "reconcile_hint_secs": "900"
 }
 ```

 jess: small nit: please keep booleans as strings for Private SDK compatibility ("true"/"false") and keep lease as a single string. we've seen nested objects break air-gapped parsers.

 marco: operational note: when an auto_unpin triggers because of alert_policy_id, runtime must emit an audit record with reason_code (e.g. ALERT_SEVERE, LEASE_EXPIRED), trigger_alerts list, observed_metrics_ref, rollout_snapshot_ref. not in primary metadata.

 srv-bot: NOTICE: rollout accepted for redwood/gptx-6b@v2 by rachel at 4065432100. cohorts: canary(5%), eu(30%).

 rachel: also propose ttl_jitter be expressed two ways: absolute jitter_secs and percent (max_pct). runtime computes jitter = min(jitter_secs, ttl*max_pct). default small: 60s or 2%.

 tom: sounds good. another edge: if owner_signature_ref points to a signed artifact that later gets revoked, do we immediately disable auto_unpin? need a revocation cadence. maybe rely on audit-store TTL + reconcile job to re-evaluate signatures periodically.

 jess: agree, add 'signature_revocation_check_secs' (default 86400) and document that revocation changes don't do immediate action; they cause the next reconcile to treat owner_signature as missing. this avoids surprises.

 marco: add a validation rule: server rejects writes where cohorts for same locality exceed 100% and reject invalid jitter values. also canonicalize cohort names to lowercase/hyphen only.

 rachel: good. I'll add an appendix to the rollout metadata RFC that includes: compact example, precedence table, jitter formula, owner_signature lifecycle, and audit-event schema pointer. Can someone volunteer to draft the runbook for emergency manual-unpin and forced-patch when signature revocation happens?

 jess: I'll draft the runbook. include CLI snippets and a checklist for forced-fallback.

 tom: I'll add unit tests for jitter calculation and signature revocation handling.

 rachel: thanks. I'll open the PR tonight with compact schema and tag you all. :raised_hands:
